correctness.rationale: On an m-chain, meet- and join-preservation amount to monotonicity with the prescribed endpoint fixes. Dunn D1 with Diamond(1)<1 forces Box≡1; D2 then forces Diamond≡0. In the alternative Diamond(1)=1, D2 with its second argument 1 forces Box(x)≤Diamond(x), hence Box(0)=0; both operators then fix endpoints. Conversely, case division on order of arguments proves both Dunn inequalities for any endpoint-fixed monotone Box≤Diamond. Interior values form a 2×(m−2) plane partition of height m−1; MacMahon yields (2m−3)Cat(m−2)Cat(m−1) normal expansions plus one exceptional pair. The claimed asymptotic follows by Catalan asymptotics. Independent exhaustive check (not executing source code) enumerated all monotone endpoint-constrained pairs and inequalities for m=2..5: 2,7,51,491, and verified each classified case. These finite checks corroborate, do not replace, the symbolic theorem.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration only through m=5; m≥2 and asymptotics rest on the chain argument and MacMahon identity.
The m=1 chain is excluded from the closed formula.
